rationale: Fournier et al. (2001) first characterized NgR1 (basis of AXER-204/NgR310ecto-Fc) binding to Nogo-66 with Kd ~5 nM; later patent (US7541335) cites this value, predating MAG/OMgp-specific affinity reports.
EP1313769A2 (published 2003-05-28) by Novartis discloses ACZ885 (canakinumab) has a KD for IL-1β binding of 'less than about 50 pM, e.g. about 35 pM' via BIAcore analysis.

Matsushita et al. 1998 (J Biol Chem) measured Scatchard-derived Kd of the 116-kDa C. histolyticum ColH collagenase (component of AA4500/CCH) binding insoluble collagen, reported in later reviews as ~10^-6 M (~1000 nM).

measure: No KD/IC50/EC50 binding affinity identified; literature reports only proteolytic degradation assays (ELISA/immunostaining) of fibronectin/laminin by microplasmin, not a binding constant
rationale: 2009 papers (e.g., Current Eye Research 34:12) measure microplasmin-induced degradation of fibronectin/laminin, not a quantitative binding affinity (KD/IC50/EC50) for these substrates.

Review cites Zia-Amirhosseini et al. 1999 (JPET) reporting SB-240563/mepolizumab binds IL-5 with picomolar affinity and IC50<1nM; exact original numeric value not directly retrievable, so approximate ~100pM used.
Medarex patent WO2006/121168 (filed 2005, published 2006) discloses Biacore SPR binding data for anti-PD-1 clone 5C4 (nivolumab/MDX-1106 precursor), later cited as ~2.6 nM KD for human PD-1.

De Weers et al. (J Immunol 2011) first characterized daratumumab (HuMax-CD38) binding to CD38, reporting high-affinity, low-nanomolar KD via Biacore/cell-binding assays, predating all later publications on this antibody.

Pre-2009 KW-0761 reports (2007 ASH abstracts, phase I trials) describe clinical activity but no numeric Kd/IC50. Quantitative CCR4 binding affinity for KW-0761 first appears in Ishii et al., Clin Cancer Res 2010.

Cenegermin is recombinant human NGF (identical sequence to native β-NGF). Kaplan et al. (1991, Science) first reported high-affinity binding of NGF to trk (TrkA/NTRK1) with Kd ≈0.1 nM in transfected cells.
Deckert et al. 2014 Clin Cancer Res reports SAR650984 (isatuximab) binds human CD38 with apparent Kd of 0.2 nmol/L, measured in binding assay, published before 2017 cutoff.
FDA review cites SPR Kd (SensiQ, Study 2010122301, run in 2010) but this was only disclosed publicly in the 2019 FDA document; no peer-reviewed or public report of the Kd value by 2012 was found.

measure: KD (receptor binding, reported as lower affinity vs rhGH)
rationale: MOD-4023 (somatrogon) was first disclosed in Prolor patents filed 2009 but published 2011+; earliest publication with measured GHR binding affinity data is the 2016 Mol. Pharmaceutics characterization paper.

Searches found AMG157/tezepelumab described as human anti-TSLP IgG2 mAb in pre-2012 clinical documents, but no quantitative KD/IC50 value was located before 2012; first explicit KD reported in 2017 structural study (Nature Communications).
Search access was exhausted before locating a pre-2008 affinity value; only later structural/binding data (e.g., Rontalizumab Fab–IFN-α2 complex, PDB 4Z5R, ~2015) were found in available results.

Hanferon is a trade-name recombinant interferon product; no publication (PubMed, patents, journals) was found reporting a measured KD/IC50/EC50 for 'Hanferon' specifically binding IFNAR1/IFNAR2, despite repeated searches.

Gillies et al. 2011 (Clin Cancer Res) report NHS-IL2LT (selectikine) proliferation/binding potency on high-affinity IL-2R+ Kit-225 cells only 4–5 fold reduced vs free IL-2 (~pM range), the earliest quantitative affinity data found, predating 2013 cutoff.
Searches found only qualitative claims that BI-1206 is a 'high-affinity' FcγRIIB antibody; no specific numeric KD/IC50/EC50 value published by 2017 could be located or verified.

Thompson et al. 2001 (Protein Eng.) described the bivalent anti-CD3 immunotoxin DT390-bisFv(UCHT1), precursor to A-dmDT390-bisFv(UCHT1)/resimmune, reporting Scatchard-derived sub-nanomolar CD3ε affinity; exact value uncertain, unverifiable via search this session.}}</br>{
Eli Lilly's EP1937721A2 (anti-IL-23 antibodies, priority 2005, published ~2008) discloses KD ~300 pM (0.3 nM) by SPR for murine parent MAb3A8, precursor to humanized LY2525623, binding IL-23 p19.
WO2015148984A2 (Ruiyi Inc., publ. 2015-10-01) reports PA13R3-P1C4, the parental clone of nimacimab (RYI-018), binding human CB1 with KD=40.54 nM, predating the 2018 cutoff.
No numeric KD/IC50 for AB154 (domvanalimab) vs TIGIT found by 2017; 2017 SEC DRS and 2019 AACR/SITC abstracts only state 'sub-nanomolar affinity' without a specific nM value.

Earliest confirmed KD data (mAb41/LY3016859 binding TGFA=36.5pM, EREG=346.6pM) is from Beidler et al., J Pharmacol Exp Ther, published 2014, after the 2012 cutoff; no earlier affinity data was verifiable.

Mu et al. (Diabetes, Jan 2012) describe Ambrx's site-specific PEGylated FGF21 (precursor of PEG-FGF21/BMS-986036), reporting EC50 potency in FGFR1c/KLB-dependent pERK cell assay; exact nM value not retrievable due to search tool failure.

measure: KD (Biacore/SPR off-rate and affinity data reported, exact nM value not retrievable from truncated patent excerpt)
rationale: GSK patent WO2011107480A1 (priority 2010, published 2011) reports Biacore binding kinetics (kd/KD) for humanized anti-SAP antibody variants including the clone underlying dezamizumab/GSK2398852, predating the 2016 cutoff; precise nM value could not be confirmed due to search access limits.

Secondary source (BioDrugs 2020) states the unmodified parent DARPin (precursor to MP0112/abicipar) was reported by Stahl et al. to bind VEGF-A165 with single-digit picomolar KD, published circa 2009.

Earliest identified disclosure of binding affinity data for Merck's anti-LAG3 antibody (precursor to MK-4280/favezelimab) is patent WO2016028672A1, published 2016-02-25, after the 2015 cutoff; no earlier affinity data found.

Only publications reporting the specific KD (~0.83 nM) for spartalizumab/PDR001 vs human PD-1 are the 2020 first-in-human paper; earlier abstracts (2018) mention only 'subnanomolar affinity' without a value, none found ≤2017.

Albumin human (OsrHSA/GLR1075) is recombinant human serum albumin itself, not an antibody/biologic that binds ALB as a target; no binding-affinity (KD/IC50) data exists since the drug and 'target' are identical.

Earliest located quantitative affinity (KD ≈1.7 nM, SPR) is for BaxB01, sharing imalumab/BAX69's variable region, in a 2017/2018 rat glomerulonephritis paper (PMID 29274331); no pre-2014 numeric affinity for imalumab found.
Yanamandra et al. 2013 Neuron reports HJ8.5 (parent mouse antibody of C2N-8E12/ABBV-8E12) KD = 0.3 pM for human tau via SPR, the earliest measured affinity before the 2016 cutoff.
Liu et al. 2015 PLoS ONE paper on Hu5F9-G4 reports SPR-measured KD of 8 nM for monomeric human CD47 binding, predating 2018 cutoff.

Roversi et al. 2007 (J Mol Biol, 'The structure of OMCI, a novel lipocalin inhibitor of the complement system') reports SPR-measured KD=1.0 nM (1.0x10^-9 M) for OmCI/rVA576 (nomacopan) binding C5, cited in later patents/clinical docs.

Searches found only post-2018 quantitative CLDN6 binding data for IMAB027/ASP1650 (EC50 0.36 nM, iScience 2022). A 2018 AACR abstract (#882) reports ADCC/CDC EC50 in ng/mL, not direct CLDN6 binding affinity.
WO2009035791A1 (published March 2009) reports SPR-derived KD values for anti-LOXL2 antibody AB0023 (parent of simtuzumab): batches gave KD of 6.6, 5.0, and 5.7 nM.
Earliest identified binding/affinity data for AMG181 (MEDI7183) vs α4β7 is the 2013 Pan et al. BJP pharmacology paper; no pre-2011 report of binding affinity was found despite extensive searching.
Web searches for CT-011/pidilizumab PD-1 binding affinity failed due to search tool errors; no verifiable pre-2008 published KD/IC50/EC50 value could be located for this antibody-target pair.

Earliest located binding affinity data for BYM338 (bimagrumab) to ActRIIA/ActRIIB (KD ~0.434 nM and ~0.0017 nM) comes from Lach-Trifilieff et al., published 2014; no earlier (≤2011) measured affinity data found via search.

AK001 (Allakos anti-Siglec-8 mAb) entered clinic in 2015; searches found no pre-2015 published numeric binding affinity (KD/IC50/EC50) value, only general mentions of AK001/AK002 as Siglec-8 antibodies.
MEDI6012 is recombinant human LCAT itself (an enzyme replacement), not a binder/antibody targeting LCAT as a receptor—so no 'binding affinity for LCAT' (KD/IC50/EC50) is reported in literature.
